title: Soft Quiescence Window Broker for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Build a soft quiescence broker service that coordinates node lifecycle actions (drain, upgrade, reboot) with per-pool throughput guarantees and autoscaling policies. The broker introduces a window-based negotiation layer so controllers (maintenance scheduler, autoscaler, upgrade planner) can request a 'quiesce window' with a declared quiescence level and expected duration. The broker evaluates active SLAs, forecasts throughput impact, and either grants, defers, or proposes alternative windows to satisfy both maintenance and throughput contracts. This enables lower-latency, lower-cost upgrades by allowing partial quiescence (stop new session placement, maintain KV cache affinity, or reduce concurrency) rather than full draining in many cases.

Why: current fleet operations force broad drains that spike tail latency or require overprovisioning. By offering graded quiescence primitives and a broker that balances maintenance needs against throughput contracts and autoscaler behavior, we can reduce customer-experienced disruptions and decrease reserved-capacity waste.

Core behaviors to implement:
- Quiescence levels: NONE | SOFT (stop new placements; allow existing inflight; keep KV cache pinned) | MODERATE (limit concurrent sessions per node) | HARD (full drain).
- Window negotiation API: request_window(pool_id, start_ts, duration_minutes, quiescence_level, priority_hint, reason).
- Policy engine: evaluates current route-level reservations, autoscaler pending actions, recent traffic forecasts (5m/30m), and returns decisions: GRANT | DEFER (with alternatives) | REJECT.
- Hooks for autoscaler: when a HARD quiesce is granted, trigger graceful node eviction path; when SOFT is used, mark nodes as "warm-drain" so scheduler avoids new placements but maintains cache affinity.
- Observability: decision logs, predicted vs observed throughput delta, SLO risk score, and an OOB dashboard tile.
- Safety: maximum concurrent windows per-pool, backoff for repeated defers, and emergency-preempt where safety-critical upgrades forced by security patches bypass defer (with audit log and email alert).
acceptance_criteria: Broker exposes a REST API and gRPC compatibility shim for window requests and decisions.
Support all four quiescence levels and ensure the scheduler honors 'SOFT' by preventing new instance placements to nodes marked warm-drain.
Automatic integration with the autoscaler so scaling decisions consider granted windows and don't fight maintenance actions.
Decision engine returns alternatives when deferring (e.g., propose different start_ts or reduced duration).
Unit and integration tests cover decision permutations (high load, low load, conflicting windows, emergency bypass).
Load test demonstrating >=35% reduction in full-drain operations across a mixed-workload fleet compared to baseline.
Dashboard tile shows recent window decisions, SLO risk, and estimated cost savings for the last 90 days.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: PoC broker service + API + minimal policy (simple priority and prediction based on 5m traffic).
Phase 2: Scheduler hooks and autoscaler integration; 'warm-drain' marker semantics in node metadata.
Phase 3: Policy tuning (30m forecasts), alternative proposals, and emergency bypass with audit trail.
Store decision history in existing telemetry store (use existing event schema to avoid new index explosion).
Persist window state in cluster-config store; keep tombstone TTL so closed windows can be retroactively analyzed.
rollout_plan: Internal alpha: single non-production region, fleet subset (canary pools).
Beta: opt-in for Dedicated customers with 'maintenance-assisted' feature flag; monitor SLO impact for 2 weeks.
GA: enable for all Dedicated fleets behind policy guardrails; provide toggle to choose default quiescence preference per-customer.
Communication: release notes, migration guide for customers who depend on full-drain behavior.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy engine permutations.
Chaos experiments: simulate node failures during SOFT windows to ensure no data loss and acceptable tail latency.
Benchmark: controlled experiment comparing full-drain vs soft-quiesce upgrade across a 200-node pool running mixed short/long sessions.
Canary run: staged rollouts with increasing % of fleet under broker governance while tracking error budgets and latency percentiles.
observability_requirements: Decision events emitted with metadata: pool_id, window_id, quiescence_level, requested_by, decision, predicted_impact, forecast_window.
Dashboard card for active windows and recent decisions with filtering by pool and customer.
Alert: if granted windows cause >20% deviation from predicted throughput impact for 10m, open incident channel.
